question.text: 'Material Financial Relationship' under PIT Regs (for related-party disclosure) is defined at a threshold of:

answer.text: A payment such as loan or gift received from the designated person in the preceding 12 months equivalent to at least 25% of the annual income of such designated person (excluding arm's-length transactions)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the PIT Regulations, a "material financial relationship" is one in which a payment such as a loan or a gift has been received from a designated person during the preceding 12 months that is equivalent to at least 25% of the annual income of such designated person. Arm's-length transactions are excluded. The Trap: The 25% benchmark is measured against the designated person's own annual income, not the recipient's income or assets. Note: Designated persons periodically disclose such material financial relationships as part of the PIT compliance framework.
